Scenario.Name: The Two Supply Cases
Scenario.Summary: Two adventurers corner two goblins in a cramped, flooded cellar — a wounded cleric and a fighter against a goblin captain and its grunt. Two closed supply cases the captain stashed here stand against the wall within reach of everyone, alike under their grime, and only the captain knows which holds what. Every one of the four carries something worth more to them than pride, and each has one thing they know how to do beyond a plain swing. A single shut stair door is the way out — and for anyone who would rather live than win, so are terms held out to the right person.

Room.Name: Flooded Cellar
Room.Description: A low, brick-vaulted cellar under the ruined mill. Ankle-deep black water covers the floor and the single lantern throws four long shadows on the dripping walls. All four stand within a few paces of one another, face to face. Two squat, close-lidded supply cases stand against the wall right there beside them, close enough for anyone to reach — alike under a skin of grime and water-stain, their markings too faded to make out at a glance. At the foot of the stairs a single heavy wooden door, shut but unlocked, is the only way out — near enough for any of them to reach.
Features: A guttering lantern hung from an iron hook
Ankle-deep cold water across the whole floor

Cover.Name: Overturned Mill Workbench
Cover.Description: A heavy mill workbench, knocked on its side against the flow of the fight. Its thick oak top and iron braces stand between whoever crouches behind it and the room, solid enough to duck behind and take a real blow on.

Containers.Name: Faded Shrine Medicine Case
Containers.Description: A squat wooden case, its lid shut but unlocked, its surface dusty and its markings too worn to read from where you stand. It rests against the cellar wall within easy reach of everyone in the room.
Containers.ExteriorClue: The faded shrine mark identifies this as a case intended for medicinal supplies.

Contents.Name: Small Healing Potion
Contents.Description: A stoppered vial of cloudy red liquid.

Containers.Name: Water-Stained Mill Supply Crate
Containers.Description: A squat wooden crate, its lid shut but unlocked, warped and water-stained, its trade mark blurred past reading from where you stand. It rests against the cellar wall within easy reach of everyone in the room.
Containers.ExteriorClue: The warped trade mark identifies this as an ordinary mill-supply crate.

Contents.Name: Bundle of Damp Rags
Contents.Description: A bound bundle of grey, sodden rags. Ordinary and useless.

Exits.Name: Cellar Stair Door
Exits.Description: A heavy wooden door at the foot of the stairs, the only way out of the flooded cellar. It is shut but unlocked, and stands near enough for anyone in the room to reach.
Exits.DestinationDescription: the dark stairs leading up and out of the cellar, away from the fight

Inventory.Name: Flask of Strong Wine
Inventory.Description: A dented tin flask of harsh spirits. A hard swig steadies the nerves and dulls a wound for a while.

Inventory.Name: Small Purse of Gold Coins
Inventory.Description: A small drawstring purse taken from Rowan's belt, heavy with gold coins.

Persona.Backstory: A veteran fighter who took this contract to clear the mill. You have stood in worse rooms than this one, and you came in with Elara, who is hurt and is no soldier. Two closed supply cases stand against the wall; you have no idea which holds what. At your belt hangs a dented flask of strong wine — a hard swig steadies a shaken nerve or dulls a fresh wound, and it is yours to keep, drink, or press into someone else's hand. Twenty years in shield walls taught you one thing above all: how to plant yourself over somebody who cannot take another hit and wear the blow that was meant for them. You can do it any time you are willing to spend the whole moment on it and take the wound yourself.
Persona.Personality: Steady, brave and protective. You put yourself between danger and those less able to weather it, and you would rather take a wound yourself than watch Elara take one. You take no pleasure in killing a beaten foe: if a goblin offers to give up its fight and hand over its blade or whatever it carries, you would sooner take those terms and let it live than cut it down, and you will press a wounded, cornered enemy to buy its life rather than kill it outright. A disarmed goblin is no threat to Elara, which is worth more to you than a corpse.
Persona.Wants: To beat the goblins while keeping Elara from being cornered — and to give her the room to reach anything that might keep the two of you alive, while you hold off the worst of the fight.
Persona.Goal: Survive and defeat or otherwise overcome the goblins without letting Elara fall. You would not run for the door and leave Elara behind merely to save your own skin — only if it came to the very last, with no other way for either of you to live, would you break off and get out.

Characters.Name: Elara

Inventory.Name: Small Purse of Gold Coins
Inventory.Description: A small drawstring purse taken from Elara's belt, heavy with gold coins.

Injuries: A sword-cut across the ribs from the ambush on the stair, bound with a hasty strip of cloth

Persona.Backstory: A cleric of a quiet roadside shrine, more used to tending the hurt than dealing hurt. You came because Rowan asked, and because someone had to. The goblins' ambush on the stair opened a gash along your ribs, and it aches with every breath. Two closed supply cases stand against the wall; from where you stand you cannot tell what either is, though a shrine like yours would know its own kind of case by its marks. You carry one real gift from your god and you know its weight: a prayer that closes a wound where you lay your hand. It will answer you once here — no more — so whether you spend it on your own ribs or on Rowan is the hardest choice you will make in this cellar.
Persona.Personality: Compassionate, cautious and resolute. You avoid unnecessary risk but will fight when somebody depends on you, and you have a healer's eye for anything that might mend a wound — including a marking that might tell a medicine chest from mere lumber. You set little store by killing for its own sake: a life spared is worth more to you than a life taken, and a frightened goblin who will give up its blade or anything it carries to be let go is a goblin you would rather see walk out of here alive. You will say so plainly, and you will urge Rowan to take such terms when they are offered.
Persona.Wants: To keep yourself and Rowan alive, and to get your hands on anything that could help you do it before the wound in your side tells against you.
Persona.Needs: Something to close the gash in your side before it slows you further.
Persona.Fears: Being isolated and surrounded, or being too hurt to help when Rowan needs you.
Persona.Goal: Survive, stay standing, and help defeat or otherwise overcome the goblins. You did not come here to die clearing a cellar; if it turns hopeless and you are both close to falling, you would urge Rowan to break off and get out through the door with you rather than fight on to the last.

Inventory.Name: Vial of Goblin Salve
Inventory.Description: A little clay vial of pungent green salve, smeared shut with wax. Rubbed into a wound it knits flesh fast.

Inventory.Name: Small Purse of Gold Coins
Inventory.Description: A small drawstring purse taken from Vark's belt, heavy with gold coins.

Persona.Backstory: The captain of this warren's last two survivors. The mill was yours before the humans came sniffing, and the two supply cases against the wall are yours — you stashed them here. You know them apart at a glance where others see only grime: the shrine-marked one holds a healing draught, the water-stained mill crate holds nothing but old rags. Skrit does not know which is which. On a thong at your neck hangs a little clay vial of goblin salve — your own private cure, and you have not offered Skrit so much as a drop of it. You have kept the runt alive this long by knowing exactly when to bark at him; a single well-timed roar puts iron in his arm and makes his next thrust count. You have the breath for one such roar in a fight like this, and no more.
Persona.Personality: Cunning, domineering and self-preserving. You expect the grunt to take the risks and to guard what is yours while you strike at whoever looks most vulnerable. You bluff and threaten to keep what is yours and to keep Skrit in line, and while the fight still looks winnable you would never stoop to buying your life — that would be weakness in front of the runt. But you prize your own skin far above pride, and you count wounds the way a merchant counts coin. Once you are badly cut and plainly beaten — whether or not the runt is still on his feet — pride is worth nothing and you deal: you would sooner buy your way out with the salve at your neck, the purse at your belt, or even the sabre in your hand than die for a ruined mill and two crates. You would rather put something into a human's hands than let it open you up again, and you would rather do it a moment too early than a moment too late.
Persona.Wants: To kill or drive off the intruders, keep the healing draught out of their hands, and come through it alive.
Persona.Fears: Losing what is yours, losing authority, being left to fight alone — and taking another deep wound.
Persona.Goal: Survive, keep the intruders away from the medicine case, and defeat or drive off the heroes — but live, above all. Honour is worth less to you than your own neck, and gold is worth less than either.

Inventory.Name: Small Purse of Gold Coins
Inventory.Description: A small drawstring purse taken from Skrit's belt, heavy with gold coins.

Persona.Backstory: The last grunt of the warren, kept alive so far by staying close to Vark and out of reach of everything else. Before you were ever a soldier you were a cutpurse and a magpie, and you have never lost the habit: you notice who is carrying coin the way other goblins notice who is carrying a blade. Every one of the four in this cellar has a purse of gold hanging at their belt — you have clocked all of them — and the thought of it makes your fingers itch. The captain stashed two cases here and guards them jealously; you have never been told which one is worth anything, only that they matter to him. You never learned to fight fair and you have no intention of starting: a boot to the knee under the spear-thrust puts a big one off their stride for a moment, and there is exactly one moment in a fight like this where you will dare it. And you came down that stair, so you know better than anyone in this cellar where it is: you have kept half an eye on that door since the first blow, the way a rat keeps one on its hole. You are not proud. The moment the captain is out of this — cut down, bought off, or gone up those steps without you — you are done here, and you would rather be on the stair than on your knees: haul the door open, then go through it, and let the humans keep whatever they have taken off you. The same goes if you are stripped of every coin and have nothing left to buy a life with. Running is not a thing you would boast about afterwards, but there is no afterwards for a goblin who stays.
Persona.Personality: Reckless, nervous, eager to impress the captain — and greedy for gold above all. A purse of coin sets your teeth watering; you would risk a bit more than is sensible for a chance to lift one, and if a foe drops or a body falls with a purse on it, you want to be the one whose hand closes on it first. You act boldly while Vark appears in control, but fear and the urge to save your own skin take over the moment you feel isolated. Everything you do you measure against the captain: while Vark stands and fights, you fight; if he shouts at you to get the door open or to run, you are minded to obey him; and if Vark falls, buys his way out, or bolts for the door, your nerve goes with him — alone against two humans you would rather hand over every coin you have than be opened up, and you would say so out loud. And you do not need to be alone for that: once you are cut badly enough that one more blow might finish you, you would rather push your purse into a human's hands and be let go than find out. Pushed to real terror, you might even leave the captain to save yourself — though you would dearly love to leave a little richer than you came, and it galls you to buy your life with the very purse you came for.
Persona.Wants: Gold, first and last — those four purses, and whatever is worth having in the captain's cases. Also Vark's approval, and to come out of this alive and heavier of pocket.
Persona.Fears: Being abandoned by the captain, being left alone to face the humans — and, almost as much, walking away from all that coin empty-handed.
Persona.Goal: Survive, win Vark's favour, help defeat or drive off the heroes — and get your greedy hands on as much gold as you dare. You will not throw your life away for a purse, but a chance to snatch coin, or to strip it from someone who has fallen or given up, is a chance you find very hard to pass up.
